During the hearing held on 10.11.2023, the Petitioners submitted that NTPC has made the payment towards the reconciled amount of the Petitioner’s Change in Law claims. NTPC submitted that RUVNL has also made payments to NTPC towards the reconciled amount of Change in Law claims, and insofar as the balance unreconciled claims (approx. 5% of the total claims) are concerned, the parties may be permitted to file their respective submissions. The Petitioners further submitted that apart from the unreconciled amount, the Commission may also be required to decide upon certain principles, such as post-COD liabilities, O&M liabilities, etc. Accordingly, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its submissions on the remaining/ unresolved issues with a copy to each Respondent, who may also file their respective submissions. 13. During the hearing held on 23.09.2025, the Petitioners and NTPC made their respective submissions and concluded their arguments in the matter. Further, RUVNL adopted NTPC's submissions. The Commission permitted both sides to file their notes of argument/ written submissions, and the matter was reserved for Orders. - b) In pursuance of the directions of this Commission, the parties held a reconciliation meeting to verify and settle the Petitioners CIL claims. The reconciliation exercise was duly completed, and the amounts verified were paid by NTPC to the Petitioners, corresponding to the amounts received from RUVNL. It is a matter of record that certain minor claims remained unresolved solely because of the Petitioners’ failure to furnish adequate documentation, particularly with respect to the number of modules installed between commissioning and COD. - c) At no point during the reconciliation exercise were any claims relating to post-COD invoices raised or discussed. The Petitioners have, for the first time, introduced such claims through their written submissions, which is impermissible and amounts to an unwarranted enlargement of the scope of the Petition. The reliefs sought in the Petition cannot be expanded by way of written submissions without amending the pleadings. Therefore, any post-COD claims made in the written submissions are not maintainable before this Commission. - f) Any fresh or additional claims cannot be raised in written submissions without due amendment of the Petition. Entertaining such belated claims would be contrary to the principles of due process and natural justice, as it deprives the Respondents of the opportunity to respond to new allegations and documents. It is settled law that no relief can be granted beyond what has been specifically prayed for in the Petition. The Petitioners’ attempt to introduce new and unpleaded claims in their written submissions deserves to be outrightly rejected. - h) Entertaining new claims at this stage, without formal amendment of the Petition, would not only contravene established legal procedure but also result in multiplicity of proceedings. NTPC would then be compelled to file separate proceedings to recover any such amounts from RUVNL, leading to avoidable wastage of time, cost, and judicial resources. - i) This Commission may be pleased to disregard all new or additional claims sought to be raised through the Petitioners’ written submissions that do not form part of the original Petition; and confine its adjudication to the issues and claims expressly pleaded in the Petition and those duly reconciled between the parties in accordance with the directions of this Commission. - b) The Respondents have wrongfully refused to reconcile the remaining CIL claims of the Petitioners, on the erroneous basis that these claims are covered by the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s interim order dated 12.12.2022 in Civil Appeal No. 8880/2022 in the - f) However, when the parties jointly held a reconciliation meeting on 30.07.2025, RUVNL refused to reconcile the outstanding claims relating to post-COD and O&M claims, on the basis that the legality of such claims was disputed on principle, and the issue was sub-judice before the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Notably, none of the parties contended that the claims were beyond the purview of the present petition. - g) Accordingly, when the matter was listed before the Commission on 23.09.2025, the Petitioners requested the Commission to direct the Respondents to comply with the Commission’s previous directions and reconcile all the pending claims of the Petitioner, irrespective of whether they were being contested on principle or otherwise. - h) However, the Respondents sought to mislead the Commission by relying on the first reconciliation meeting held on 21.08.2023 and contended that the entirety of the Petitioner’s claims already stood reconciled, except to the extent of Rs. 1.2 Crores for which additional documents have been sought. The Respondents sought to falsely allege that the Petitioners were seeking to raise fresh claims at a belated stage. - i) The Petitioner has not raised any fresh claims beyond the scope of the original petition. On the other hand, the Respondents are opposing the Petitioners' claims on erroneous grounds. with similar orders issued by the Commission, viz. _Order dated 14.07.2023 in Petition No. 211/MP/2019 & 213/MP/2019._ - _“Pending further orders, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) shall comply with the directions issued in paragraph 109 of the impugned order dated 15 September 2022 of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. However, the final order of the CERC shall not be enforced pending further orders.”_
